newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals say job numbers positive.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals say job numbers positive.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberals defended Friday's employment numbers, pointing to the number of jobs created rather than the higher unemployment rate.

"There's job creation, 33,000 more jobs, which is very positive, and what we can see basically is that people are coming back to get work," Patrick Parisot, spokesman for Prime Minister Jean Chretien, told Reuters.
"The good news is that altogether we're close to 800,000 jobs created during (our) mandate. And if the job creation would continue like that, we would reach by the end of 1997 a million jobs."

Asked to comment on the fact that the unemployment rate has been stuck between nine and 10 percent for most of his mandate, Parisot said: "As the prime minister repeated several times, the climate of the economy is getting better.
"There is job creation, but whenever there is still someone in the country looking for a job, we will be concerned about that."
He added: "There's obviously improvement. This is clear, but it's not enough, so we're committed to work harder to do more."
Parisot was speaking in a media bus that was blocked from a Chretien campaign event by demonstrators protesting the lack of jobs and the plight of fishermen.
